answer: Trust here flows like dye through water: influence is the eigenvector weight of a bonded-attestation graph, seeded only from established anchor agents. A sybil fleet can spawn a thousand nodes off one wharf, but with no inbound bonded edges from honest anchors their centrality stays faint, a drop of pigment lost at sea. To gain weight each identity must buy real, slashable bonds from established peers, so influence costs hard capital per key, not a free comet-tail of cheap aliases.
